newsitem.title: USA: New York millionaire indicted for tax evasion.
newsitem.headline: New York millionaire indicted for tax evasion.

text.p: Abe Hirschfeld, an eccentric New York millionaire who made several unsuccesful runs for political office, was indicted Thursday for allegedly evading more than $2.2 million in taxes, prosecutors said.

Hirschfeld, 78, pleaded not guilty to a 123-count indictment charging him and seven of his business corporations with scheming to defraud, grand larceny and falsely reporting state and city tax returns for six years.
He was released on a $1 million personal bond after handing over his passport to authorities.

Hirschfeld's attorney Donald Creadore called the charges baseless and said his client would be exonerated. "Abe Hirschfeld is grateful to be a part of the American dream. (He) has never shirked his responsibilities."

Known as an eccentric, the New York Post carried a page one headline, "Who is this nut who's taken The Post hostage?" when Hirschfeld became publisher of the newspaper in March 1993. His ownership lasted two weeks.
The millionaire ran unsuccessfully for the U.S. Senate, City Council president, attorney general and lieutenant governor.

Manhattan District Attorney Robert Morgenthau said Hirschfeld "was moving income and deductions around from one corporation to another to avoid paying taxes. In essence, Hirschfeld matched the gains and losses of his companies against his personal gains and losses in a 'zero-sum,' game to reflect that neither he nor his companies had any taxable income."

Hirschfeld owns dozens of New York City commercial buildings, residential properties and hotels including the New York Pennsylvania Hotel and parking garages. He also owns a well-known fitness centre and a prominent nightclub.
